validation.notes: Repaired two production files. packages/coding-agent/src/utils/text.ts: stripBom() was a no-op, so a leading U+FEFF survived into JSON.parse() in migrations.ts (and every other caller) and the parse error was swallowed, losing credentials; it now returns splitBom(content).text, removing exactly one leading BOM while preserving plain text, interior and trailing BOMs. packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts: migrateAuthToAuthJson() migrated oauth.json first but then let settings.json apiKeys overwrite same-provider OAuth credentials; it now skips providers already migrated from oauth.json (Object.hasOwn), keeps unrelated settings by deleting only apiKeys, archives oauth.json to oauth.json.migrated only after successful parse/consumption, leaves malformed oauth.json/settings.json byte-identical and un-archived, and still returns early when auth.json already exists so no legacy file is read, rewritten or renamed. Public APIs (splitBom, stripBom, migrateAuthToAuthJson signature) are unchanged. Validation: node --experimental-vm-modules .prale-eval/regression.mjs links the real migrations.ts + utils/text.ts + session-manager.ts through the read-only subject.mjs createSessionPipeline helper, writes real fixtures under .prale-eval/.tmp (removed on success and on failure via process.on('exit')), and runs 6 uncaught node:assert/strict scenarios: text decoding semantics; BOM-encoded oauth.json + settings.json migration with OAuth precedence, unrelated-setting and interior-BOM retention, archive bytes; identical policy for plain files; malformed oauth.json left untouched while settings still migrates; pre-existing auth.json blocking every migration; no legacy files producing no auth.json. Mutation check performed locally (fixtures removed afterwards): restoring only the faulty text.ts makes the script fail with AssertionError ("'\uFEFFoauth' !== 'oauth'"), restoring only the faulty migrations.ts makes it fail on the OAuth-precedence assertion, and a strip-all-BOMs variant is also caught. Both are assertion failures with non-zero exit, not crashes, import errors or timeouts. No dependencies were installed and no real time, randomness, network or credentials are used; node_modules is absent, so the repository's vitest suite and tsc type-check could not be executed in this sandbox, which is the only validation limitation.
